hero.headline: Trump names housing regulator Bill Pulte acting director of national intelligence
hero.body:
President Trump has appointed Bill Pulte, head of the Federal Housing Finance Agency, to serve as acting director of national intelligence. Pulte will retain his position overseeing the FHFA while taking on one of the nation's most sensitive security roles.

The appointment came days after Tulsi Gabbard departed from the intelligence director position. Trump announced the decision on his Truth Social platform, stating that "William has deep experience managing the most sensitive matters in America."

Pulte, an heir to a home construction company fortune and major Republican donor, has no known background in national security or intelligence work. His prominence in the Trump administration stems from his role at the FHFA, the agency that regulates Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, which together back approximately half of all U.S. mortgages.

During his tenure at the housing agency, Pulte has made public allegations against several of Trump's political opponents. He has accused Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook of mortgage fraud, charges Cook has denied. He also played a role in Trump's campaign against former Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell.

The dual appointment represents an extraordinary concentration of responsibility. The director of national intelligence coordinates work across 18 intelligence agencies and serves as the president's primary intelligence adviser. The position, created after the September 11 attacks to improve coordination across the intelligence community, has historically demanded exclusive focus given its scope and sensitivity.

Democratic Senator Mark Warner, vice-chairman of the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, criticized the appointment. "Rather than selecting a respected national security professional capable of delivering independent judgments, the president has chosen an official who has demonstrated not just willingness but eagerness to use the authorities of government to pursue political retribution," Warner said.

Warner noted that Pulte had used his FHFA authority to pursue what he characterized as the president's grievances. "Americans have already seen Mr Pulte use the powers of his office at the Federal Housing Finance Agency to pursue the president's perceived political opponents," Warner stated.

A former high-ranking official described Pulte's handling of the Cook case as "very bizarre."

The appointment occurs as the administration manages multiple foreign policy challenges, including ongoing negotiations with Iran and questions surrounding Taiwan policy. Gabbard, during her time as intelligence director, faced marginalization in the role and appeared sidelined as Trump pursued aggressive foreign policy actions.

Pulte's appointment as acting intelligence director while continuing to lead the FHFA means he will simultaneously oversee housing finance policy and manage relationships with the nation's intelligence agencies and foreign intelligence services.

cards.headline: Trump says Iran nuclear talks continue despite ceasefire breakdown
cards.teaser: The president defended ongoing negotiations with Iran, calling a deal complex as fighting persists.
cards.body:
President Trump stated that negotiations with Iran are ongoing, though he acknowledged a potential agreement would be difficult to achieve. Secretary of State Marco Rubio prepared to testify before Congress about the talks and the administration's foreign policy strategy.

Trump spoke with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in a tense conversation, urging him to reduce military operations. Following Trump's intervention, Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon killed eight people after the president said he had instructed Netanyahu to cancel an attack on Beirut. A ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah is considered essential to progress on the broader Iran peace process.

cards.headline: Secretary of State Rubio to testify before Congress as Iran ceasefire deteriorates
cards.teaser: Marco Rubio will appear publicly for the first time since hostilities began, facing lawmakers frustrated with the worsening regional conflict.
cards.body:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio will testify before Congress as the ceasefire agreement with Iran shows signs of collapse. The appearance marks his first public testimony since the war began.

The regional conflict has intensified in recent days, testing the patience of lawmakers who are demanding answers about the administration's strategy. Rubio's testimony comes at a moment when diplomatic efforts to maintain the ceasefire appear to be failing.

cards.headline: Israel Strikes Southern Lebanon After Holding Off Beirut Attack
cards.teaser: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu backed away from striking Beirut under pressure from President Trump but vowed to continue operations against Hezbollah.
cards.body:
Israel conducted military strikes in southern Lebanon while refraining from attacks on Beirut following pressure from President Trump. Prime Minister Netanyahu confirmed Israel would maintain its campaign against Hezbollah despite the restraint on expanding operations to the Lebanese capital.

The ceasefire discussions between Israel and Hezbollah, brokered with U.S. involvement, are viewed as essential to broader peace negotiations with Iran. However, clashes have continued despite both sides accepting a partial ceasefire plan. Hezbollah's drone capabilities have shifted the conflict's dynamics, challenging Israel's initial military strategy in Lebanon.

cards.headline: Russian Strikes Kill 21 in Ukraine as Rescuers Search Rubble
cards.body:
Russian forces launched a massive overnight assault on Ukraine, firing 73 missiles and 656 drones at multiple cities including Kyiv, Dnipro, Zaporizhzhia, Poltava and Kharkiv. The bombardment killed at least 21 people and left dozens injured, with rescue workers continuing to search through rubble for additional casualties.

Among the dead were an eight-year-old boy and other civilians killed when residential buildings were struck. In Dnipro, a three-year-old boy was buried when a four-storey apartment block collapsed. Rescue operations continued in the early morning hours as workers pulled bodies from debris.

The scale of the attack was significant. Ukraine's air defences intercepted approximately half of the missiles fired, but more than 30 struck civilian targets. In Kyiv, six people died and 66 were injured, including three children. A 24-storey apartment block was hit, triggering a collapse. Other buildings caught fire, including a nine-storey block, and vehicles were damaged by falling debris. Power was cut for 140,000 residents, though utility workers later restored electricity to 110,000.

In Dnipro, at least 12 people were killed and 37 injured. Six people remained missing under the rubble, and a rescuer was killed in a second strike. The mayor accused Russia of deliberately using cluster munitions in residential areas to maximize civilian casualties. In Kharkiv, at least 14 people were injured and numerous homes and vehicles were damaged.

The attack prompted Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to appeal directly to Donald Trump for Patriot missiles. Zelenskyy has repeatedly stated that Ukraine is running out of Patriot interceptors, which are needed to defend against the ballistic and hypersonic missiles Russia is using. He described them as "vital tools" in protecting civilian lives and noted that ballistic missiles represent Moscow's "last major advantage on the battlefield."

The Trump administration has not responded to Zelenskyy's requests. The Patriot systems are in short supply globally after hundreds were used in the February conflict between the United States and Iran.

Ukrainian officials framed the strikes as evidence of Russian desperation. Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha stated that Russia is losing on the battlefield and that "no number of missiles can change this." He accused Putin of using terror as his remaining option after Ukraine's recent successes in aerial campaigns, including strikes on Russian oil refineries and ports.

The assault came after Zelenskyy had warned residents to heed air raid alerts, indicating that intelligence suggested a major strike was being prepared. Rescue operations continued as residents sheltered in basements, corridors and metro stations throughout the affected cities.

cards.headline: Hezbollah Drones Shift Israeli Military Strategy in Lebanon
cards.teaser: An Israeli military campaign that began with high expectations has stalled as Hezbollah demonstrates greater capability than when the war started.
cards.body:
Hezbollah's drone capabilities have forced Israel to reassess its military approach in Lebanon. What began as an Israeli campaign with significant objectives has stalled into a stalemate, with Hezbollah demonstrating greater strength than when the conflict began. The group's drones have successfully breached Israeli air defenses, posing threats to northern Israeli territory including the city of Haifa. An Israeli military physician was killed in a drone strike, with seven others injured in the same attack.

A ceasefire framework has been proposed with U.S. involvement, though clashes continue despite both sides accepting a partial cessation of hostilities. Regional diplomacy has intensified, with Iran suspending talks with the United States over Israeli military operations in Lebanon and Gaza.

cards.headline: Trump Announces 25% Tariff on Brazilian Imports
cards.body:
The Trump administration announced a 25% tariff on imports from Brazil, citing what it calls unfair trade practices. The proposal represents the latest in a series of tariff actions as the administration seeks to rebuild its trade enforcement agenda through Section 301 investigations.

Section 301 refers to a provision of the Trade Act of 1974 that allows the United States to investigate and respond to foreign trade practices deemed unfair or discriminatory. The administration has increasingly relied on this mechanism to justify tariffs and other trade restrictions on countries it believes are not trading fairly with American companies.

Brazil is a significant trading partner of the United States, with bilateral trade in goods totaling billions of dollars annually. The country exports a wide range of products to the United States, including steel, aircraft, agricultural goods, and machinery. A 25% tariff would substantially increase costs for American importers and could affect prices for consumers and businesses that rely on Brazilian products.

The tariff announcement comes as the administration has pursued an aggressive trade policy focused on reducing trade deficits and protecting domestic industries. Previous tariff actions have targeted countries including China, Canada, Mexico, and members of the European Union. Some of these tariffs have prompted retaliatory measures from trading partners, leading to disputes that have affected various sectors of the American economy.

The proposal will likely face scrutiny from American businesses that import Brazilian goods, as well as from Brazil itself, which may consider counter-measures. Trade groups representing importers and manufacturers have previously opposed broad tariff increases, arguing they raise costs for American companies and consumers.

This announcement arrives as the Trump administration faces ongoing disputes over its earlier tariff policies. The Supreme Court previously struck down some of Trump's tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, leading to a refund process for roughly 330,000 importers who paid more than $166 billion in fees. Federal agencies have now established a refund process allowing businesses to recover tariff costs through their original customs brokers, with refunds expected within 60 to 90 days.

Major shipping companies have responded to the tariff refund process by pledging to return funds to customers. FedEx and UPS have committed to sharing refunds, while DHL is doing the same. However, larger retailers including Amazon, Apple, and Costco have remained silent on whether they will pass refund money along to their customers.

The implementation timeline and any potential exemptions for the new Brazilian tariff have not been detailed in the announcement. Trade groups and business organizations are expected to respond with concerns about the economic impact on supply chains and consumer prices.

cards.headline: Court Blocks U.S. Ebola Quarantine Unit in Kenya
cards.teaser: A Kenyan court further delayed plans for a Trump administration quarantine facility for Americans exposed to Ebola, a project that has sparked protests.
cards.body:
A Kenyan court has halted the Trump administration's plan to establish a quarantine facility for Americans exposed to Ebola. The proposed medical unit would house U.S. citizens who contracted or were exposed to the virus while working or traveling in affected regions.

The facility has sparked significant public opposition in Kenya, with demonstrations occurring near the proposed site. The court ruling represents another major obstacle to the U.S. effort to move forward with the project.

cards.headline: South African Police Investigate Killing of Two Mozambican Men
cards.teaser: Two Mozambican men were killed following violent protests against illegal migration in the coastal town of Mossel Bay.
cards.body:
South African police opened an investigation into the deaths of two Mozambican men in Mossel Bay. The killings occurred after a day of violent protests targeting illegal migration in the town.

Mossel Bay, located on South Africa's southern coast, has experienced rising tensions over migration in recent months. The protests escalated into violence before the two men were killed, prompting the police investigation.

cards.headline: Lebanon Caught Between U.S., Israel and Iran as Conflict Escalates
cards.teaser: Lebanon has been hit by military strikes but has little say in determining its future as larger powers negotiate.
cards.body:
Lebanon endures military strikes while remaining largely excluded from diplomatic negotiations shaping its future. International powers conduct operations with Lebanon as the backdrop, leaving the country to face consequences of decisions made elsewhere.

Israel and Hezbollah have accepted a U.S. partial ceasefire plan, though clashes continue. A cessation of hostilities between the two groups is viewed as crucial to broader peace efforts involving Iran. President Trump has pressured Israeli leadership to hold back from attacking Beirut, though Israel vows to continue its campaign against Hezbollah.

cards.headline: Ghana President to Review Anti-LGBTQ Bill Before Approval
cards.teaser: A bill passed by Ghanaian lawmakers would impose prison sentences for people identifying as LGBTQ.
cards.body:
Ghana's parliament has passed legislation that would criminalize LGBTQ+ identification and activities, with penalties of three to 10 years imprisonment. President John Dramani Mahama has said the bill will be reviewed before he takes action on approval.

Rights groups warn the law has sparked fear within Ghana's LGBTQ+ community, with concerns about potential loss of employment, housing, and access to healthcare if it becomes law.

hero.headline: Seven family members dead in Iowa shooting
hero.body:
Police in Muscatine, Iowa, say a man shot and killed six relatives before taking his own life in what authorities are investigating as a murder-suicide. The incident left seven people dead total.

Law enforcement responded to the scene in Muscatine, a city of roughly 23,000 residents located about 170 miles east of Des Moines along the Mississippi River in eastern Iowa. The suspected shooter was found dead near a bridge with a self-inflicted gunshot wound, according to authorities.

Police believe the suspected gunman was responsible for all six deaths before dying by suicide. Authorities have not released the names of the victims or the suspected gunman. The shooting occurred at a location where the family members were present together. Investigators are working to piece together the timeline of events and circumstances that led to the deaths.

The Muscatine school district issued a response following the incident, acknowledging the impact on the local community. Law enforcement agencies are continuing their investigation into the details surrounding the shooting.

This shooting represents one of the deadliest incidents involving multiple family members in Iowa in recent memory. The incident has drawn attention to the broader issue of domestic violence and family-related homicides across the country.

Police are working with local officials to provide support to those affected by the deaths. The investigation remains active as authorities gather evidence and interview witnesses to understand what may have motivated the shooting and whether there were any warning signs prior to the incident.

cards.headline: Trump names Bill Pulte acting director of national intelligence
cards.teaser: The president has appointed a housing regulator to lead intelligence operations, replacing Tulsi Gabbard.
cards.body:
President Trump has appointed Bill Pulte as acting director of national intelligence, replacing Tulsi Gabbard who recently stepped down from the role. Pulte currently heads the Federal Housing Finance Agency.

Pulte is an heir to a home construction company fortune and has served as a housing regulator within the Trump administration. His appointment to lead the nation's top intelligence agency represents a significant leadership change at the Office of the Director of National Intelligence.

cards.headline: Rubio testifies before Congress on Iran policy
cards.teaser: Secretary of State Marco Rubio faces lawmakers as the ceasefire with Iran shows signs of collapse.
cards.body:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio appeared before Congress to discuss the Trump administration's Iran policy and foreign affairs strategy. The hearing took place as a ceasefire agreement with Iran showed signs of deteriorating, raising concerns about potential military escalation.

Lawmakers questioned Rubio about the administration's approach to negotiations with Iran and its handling of the ongoing conflict. The testimony represented Rubio's first congressional appearance since hostilities with Iran began.

cards.headline: Californians vote in tight governor primary
cards.teaser: Voters are deciding between candidates seeking to succeed Governor Gavin Newsom in a race too close to call.
cards.body:
California residents are voting in a competitive primary election to select the top two candidates for governor. The race has drawn significant attention as Democrats determine the party's direction in the state.

Multiple states are holding primaries simultaneously, including Iowa, Montana, New Jersey, South Dakota and New Mexico. The California governor's race involves competing visions on issues including housing, public safety and economic policy.

cards.headline: Los Angeles voters choose mayoral candidates in primary
cards.teaser: Mayor Karen Bass faces challenges from Kevin Pratt and Nithya Raman in the city's primary election.
cards.body:
Los Angeles residents are voting in a mayoral primary featuring incumbent Karen Bass, reality television figure Spencer Pratt, and City Council member Nithya Raman. The race has focused on economic concerns and institutional problems facing the city.

Pratt has campaigned on promises to disrupt what he describes as systemic dysfunction in Los Angeles government. His candidacy has brought attention to voter frustration with the city's direction. The primary will determine which candidates advance to a general election runoff.

cards.headline: Jill Biden says doctors examined president after debate
cards.teaser: The former first lady revealed in a new book that medical staff checked Joe Biden immediately following his appearance.
cards.body:
Jill Biden reveals in her new memoir that doctors examined President Biden immediately following his debate with Donald Trump. The former first lady expressed concern that he may have suffered a stroke, prompting the urgent medical evaluation.

The disclosure contradicts the Biden administration's earlier public statements, which indicated that doctors examined the president several days after the debate rather than in the immediate aftermath.

cards.headline: Administration Proposes Blocking Grants Over Political Alignment
cards.teaser: A new proposal would allow the administration to block federal grants if recipients do not support the president's agenda.
cards.body:
New Proposal Would Allow Administration to Block Grants if They Don't Support Trump's Agenda

The administration has proposed giving the government authority to block federal grants to organizations based on political alignment with President Trump's agenda or what officials describe as anti-American values. The proposal would apply to grant applications and ongoing grants across agencies that fund scientific research, education, infrastructure, and social services.

The decision could affect universities, nonprofits, state and local governments, and private organizations receiving federal funding. The proposal raises questions about how the administration will define which values qualify as anti-American or which grant recipients adequately support the presidential agenda.

cards.headline: Alphabet Stock Drags on Market After Record Highs
cards.teaser: The S&P 500 traded near flat as shares of Alphabet declined, slowing a record-breaking rally.
cards.body:
Alphabet announced plans to raise up to $80 billion through an equity offering to fund artificial intelligence infrastructure investments. The fundraising, the largest equity capital raise ever recorded, includes a $10 billion investment from Berkshire Hathaway. The move underscores the substantial capital requirements driving the AI sector's expansion.

The announcement comes as Anthropic, maker of the Claude chatbot, filed confidentially for an initial public offering. Anthropic was recently valued at $965 billion following a $65 billion funding round, reflecting the intensifying competition and investment in AI companies.

cards.headline: Victoria's Secret Shares Jump 35% on Turnaround Results
cards.teaser: The lingerie retailer reported strong bra sales and raised its annual forecast, sending shares sharply higher.
cards.body:
Victoria's Secret shares surged 35% after the company reported results showing its turnaround efforts are gaining traction. Strong bra sales powered the quarter's performance, beating earnings and revenue estimates. The company also raised its outlook for the full year, signaling confidence in continued momentum.

The results mark a significant shift for the retailer, which has worked to revitalize its brand and product offerings. The stock jump represents one of the largest single-day gains for the company in recent years. Victoria's Secret has focused on updating its marketing approach and product lines to appeal to changing consumer preferences in the lingerie market.

cards.headline: Mellon Heir Transfers $5.5 Million Estate to Kennedy Nonprofit
cards.teaser: A Trump megadonor gave Connecticut properties covering 300 acres to Robert F. Kennedy Jr.'s Children's Health Defense at no cost.
cards.body:
A member of the Mellon family transferred an estate valued at $5.5 million to Children's Health Defense, a nonprofit led by Robert F. Kennedy Jr., last year. The transfer included adjacent Connecticut properties totaling about 300 acres and was made at no cost to the organization. The donor is described as a major contributor to Trump's political efforts.

Children's Health Defense has been a prominent organization in debates over public health policy. The substantial real estate donation provides the nonprofit with significant assets. The timing of the transfer, which occurred last year, places it during a period of heightened political activity around health policy issues.

cards.headline: Short-Seller Andrew Left Convicted of Securities Fraud
cards.teaser: A federal jury found the prominent investor guilty, raising concerns among others who bet against companies.
cards.body:
A federal jury convicted Andrew Left, a well-known short-seller who gained fame betting against companies, of securities fraud. The verdict has created worry among other short-sellers about the implications for their investment strategies and public commentary on stocks.

Left built his reputation by publicly questioning the valuations and business practices of various companies, then profiting when their stock prices declined. The securities fraud conviction suggests prosecutors successfully argued that his actions crossed legal boundaries. The case could affect how short-sellers communicate their research and positions going forward.

cards.headline: SpaceX Seeks to Reduce Investment Banking Fees for Potential IPO
cards.teaser: The company wants to cut fees as bankers eye a $500 million windfall from a public offering.
cards.body:
SpaceX is pushing to reduce the fees it would pay to investment banks in connection with a potential initial public offering. Bankers working on the deal are targeting approximately $500 million in fees, which SpaceX considers too high.

The dispute over fees reflects the enormous scale of a potential SpaceX IPO, which would be one of the largest public offerings in recent years. hero.headline: UN warns new El Niño could begin within weeks, pushing global temperatures higher
hero.body:
The United Nations has warned that a new El Niño weather pattern could start within weeks, adding heat to a planet already experiencing the effects of climate change. The natural phenomenon, which involves warming ocean temperatures in the Pacific, has historically contributed to increased global temperatures and extreme weather events.

El Niño occurs when warmer than average sea surface temperatures develop in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean. These conditions alter atmospheric circulation patterns, affecting weather worldwide. The phenomenon typically appears every two to seven years and lasts nine to twelve months, though some episodes have persisted for longer periods.

The timing raises concerns among climate scientists because global temperatures have already risen due to greenhouse gas emissions. When El Niño conditions combine with underlying warming trends, the result is often record-breaking heat. Previous strong El Niño events have been associated with droughts, floods, and disruptions to agriculture and water supplies across multiple continents.

The UN characterization of this potential El Niño as possibly the strongest in decades suggests the upcoming episode could produce significant temperature increases. Strong El Niño events have historically driven global average temperatures upward by fractions of a degree Celsius, which can translate into tangible impacts on weather patterns, crop yields, and water availability in vulnerable regions.

The warning comes as countries continue efforts to reduce emissions and adapt to changing climate conditions. Scientists monitor ocean temperatures and atmospheric indicators to predict El Niño development and provide advance notice to governments and communities that may face drought, flooding, or other weather extremes. The weeks ahead will determine whether the predicted pattern materializes and how strong it becomes, shaping weather and climate outcomes for much of the next year.

cards.headline: Anthropic expands security program to protect critical infrastructure in 15 countries
cards.teaser: The AI company is scaling its Mythos security system to 150 organizations overseeing power, water, healthcare, and communications networks.
cards.body:
Anthropic is expanding Project Glasswing, its security vulnerability detection program, to 150 organizations across 15 countries. The initiative grants these organizations access to Mythos and focuses on critical infrastructure sectors including power grids, water systems, healthcare facilities, and communications networks.

The program targets infrastructure where cyberattacks could potentially impact 100 million people. Project Glasswing uses AI to identify security vulnerabilities before attackers can exploit them.

cards.headline: X adds video reaction feature to posts
cards.teaser: The social media platform introduced a new way for users to respond to content with video reactions.
cards.body:
X announced a new feature that allows users to react to posts with video responses. The feature is part of the platform's effort to appeal to content creators and expand engagement options beyond text replies and standard reactions.

The video reaction tool lets users record and attach video responses directly to posts they are viewing. X has been adding creator-focused features as it competes with other social platforms for user engagement and content production.

cards.headline: Apple ships 1.1 million MacBook Neo units in opening weeks
cards.teaser: The new laptop model is helping Apple expand its presence in the mainstream computer market, according to industry estimates.
cards.body:
Apple's MacBook Neo has captured strong early demand, with IDC estimating 1.1 million units shipped during its initial weeks on sale. The laptop is helping Apple expand its reach into the mainstream market segment.

The shipment figures indicate a successful product launch for Apple's computer division as the company pursues a broader audience of buyers with the new MacBook Neo.

cards.headline: Blue Origin plans second New Glenn launch this year after explosion
cards.teaser: The space company said launchpad damage in Florida was less severe than expected following last week's rocket explosion.
cards.body:
Blue Origin CEO Dave Limp announced the company plans to launch its New Glenn rocket again this year, following last week's explosion. The damage to the company's Florida launchpad proved less severe than initially assessed.

The cause of the explosion remains undisclosed by Blue Origin. The timeline for the next launch will depend on completing necessary repairs to the facility.

cards.headline: Energy Department restarts rebate program with new restrictions on heating
cards.teaser: The program will no longer cover switching from fossil fuels to electric heating systems.
cards.body:
The Department of Energy restarted its energy rebate program with modified eligibility requirements. The revised program excludes rebates for converting heating systems from fossil fuels to electricity.

The previous version of the program provided financial incentives for homeowners to replace gas or oil heating with electric heat pumps and other electric heating systems. The change removes that category from eligible upgrades, altering the program's approach to residential energy efficiency improvements.

cards.headline: Microsoft Office 2019 for Mac will lose editing capability in July
cards.teaser: The software will shift to read-only mode, preventing users from editing or saving documents.
cards.body:
Microsoft announced that Office 2019 for Mac will stop allowing users to edit and save documents starting July 13, 2026. The software will transition to read-only mode, meaning users can open and view files but cannot make changes.

The change affects users of Office 2019 who have not upgraded to newer versions or subscription-based Microsoft 365. Users who need editing functionality will need to move to a current version of Office. The shift has generated criticism from users who purchased perpetual licenses for Office 2019.

hero.headline: Hall of Fame basketball coach Rick Adelman dies at 79
hero.body:
Rick Adelman, a Hall of Fame basketball coach who compiled more than 1,000 wins during his nearly 30-year NBA career, has died at age 79.

Adelman joined a select group of coaches who achieved the 1,000-win milestone, a distinction that reflects both sustained excellence and remarkable longevity in professional basketball. His induction into the Basketball Hall of Fame recognized his significant contributions to the sport and his place among the game's most accomplished coaches.

Throughout his tenure leading NBA teams, Adelman built a reputation for strategic thinking and an ability to construct winning rosters across different organizations. He became known for developing effective offensive systems and maximizing the potential of the players at his disposal. His influence extended beyond the teams he directly coached, shaping how players and coaches throughout the NBA approached the game.

The coaching milestone of 1,000 victories represents an exclusive achievement in league history. Only a handful of coaches have reached this benchmark, and doing so requires success across multiple decades and different organizational contexts. Adelman's ability to maintain excellence throughout such a lengthy career underscored his tactical knowledge and adaptability as the game evolved.

His Hall of Fame recognition reflected the lasting impact he made on professional basketball. Beyond his win total, Adelman's strategic innovations and player development approach influenced the broader coaching community. He demonstrated how sustained success could be built through careful roster construction and system implementation rather than reliance on any single generation of talent.

Adelman's career spanned significant changes in the NBA, from the league's expansion era through the modern era. His longevity and continued success through these different periods highlighted his ability to adjust to changing circumstances while maintaining competitive excellence. This adaptability separated him from coaches whose success proved limited to particular eras or team configurations.

The loss of Adelman marks the passing of a major figure in NBA history. His nearly three decades of coaching left a lasting imprint on professional basketball. Players who spent time under his direction often credited him with improving their understanding of the game and their individual performance. Coaches who came after him built upon principles and systems he had pioneered.

His Hall of Fame induction acknowledged what his 1,000-plus wins demonstrated: Rick Adelman was among the greatest coaches professional basketball has produced. His death removes one of the last living links to decades of NBA history and closes a chapter on one of the sport's most successful careers. His legacy will be measured both in wins and in the lasting influence he exerted on how the game is played and coached at its highest level.

cards.headline: Browns trade Myles Garrett to Rams for Jared Verse and draft picks
cards.teaser: Cleveland sent its star defensive end to Los Angeles in exchange for multiple draft picks including a 2027 first-rounder.
cards.body:
The Cleveland Browns traded star edge rusher Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams for linebacker Jared Verse and three draft picks. Garrett, 30, is a two-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year and seven-time Pro Bowl selection. Since being drafted first overall by Cleveland in 2017, he has accumulated 125.5 sacks, 413 pressures and 149 tackles for loss—more than any other player during that span.

In 2025, Garrett set the single-season sacks record with 23, making him one of the league's premier defensive players. The trade marks a significant shift for both franchises as Los Angeles adds an elite pass rusher while Cleveland receives defensive reinforcements and future draft assets.

cards.headline: Eagles trade A.J. Brown to Patriots for 2028 first-round pick
cards.teaser: Philadelphia sent its star wide receiver to New England in exchange for a 2028 first-round pick and a 2027 fifth-rounder.
cards.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles traded wide receiver A.J. Brown to the New England Patriots on Monday. In exchange, the Eagles received a first-round draft pick in 2028 and a fifth-round pick in 2027.

Brown, a three-time Pro Bowl selection, reunites with Patriots coach Mike Vrabel. The trade ends months of speculation about Brown's future with Philadelphia, where he had grown frustrated with the team.

cards.headline: Stanley Cup Final between Hurricanes and Golden Knights begins
cards.teaser: The 2026 NHL playoffs conclude with the championship series starting Tuesday.
cards.body:
The 2026 Stanley Cup Final gets underway Tuesday with the Carolina Hurricanes facing the Vegas Golden Knights. This best-of-seven series represents the culmination of the NHL playoffs, with both teams vying for the championship title.

The matchup features the Golden Knights returning to the final round, while the Hurricanes pursue their first Stanley Cup victory since 2006. Game 1 will kick off the series to determine this year's champion.

cards.headline: Texas Tech defeats Alabama twice to reach WCWS championship
cards.teaser: Pitcher NiJaree Canady led Texas Tech past the top-seeded Crimson Tide to set up a rematch with Texas in the finals.
cards.body:
Texas Tech defeated top-seeded Alabama twice on Monday night to advance to the Women's College World Series championship series. Pitcher NiJaree Canady delivered another dominant performance to propel the Red Raiders past the Crimson Tide.

Texas Tech will face Texas in the championship series, marking the first title rematch since the WCWS adopted the best-of-three format in 2005. The two in-state rivals will compete for the national championship after both teams navigated through the tournament bracket.

cards.headline: Marta Kostyuk advances to French Open semifinals
cards.teaser: The Ukrainian player upset compatriot Elina Svitolina and will face Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva next.
cards.body:
Ukraine's Marta Kostyuk defeated fellow Ukrainian Elina Svitolina in the French Open quarterfinals to reach the semifinals. Following the victory at Roland Garros, Kostyuk dedicated her win to Ukraine.

Kostyuk will face Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva in the semifinal round. Andreeva advanced to her second Grand Slam semifinal after a dominant performance against Sorana Cirstea in the quarterfinals.

cards.headline: Caitlin Clark and Stephanie White address relationship questions
cards.teaser: The Fever star and head coach insisted there are no issues between them after an animated sideline discussion.
cards.body:
Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark and head coach Stephanie White addressed speculation about their relationship on Monday following an animated exchange during Saturday's 100-84 loss to Portland. Both dismissed suggestions of any rift between them, characterizing the discussion as routine coaching.

The public clarification came after observers noted the visible interaction during the game. Clark and White's joint statement aimed to move past the weekend incident as the Fever continue their season.

hero.headline: YouTube Films Break Box Office Records, Upending Hollywood Distribution Model
hero.body:
Two horror films produced by YouTube creators opened this past weekend to combined box office success, marking what industry observers describe as a fundamental shift in how films reach audiences. The results demonstrate that established online communities can translate directly into theatrical performance without traditional studio marketing infrastructure.

Backrooms, produced for approximately $10 million and distributed by A24, earned $81 million in its opening weekend. The film originated from a 4chan creepypasta, an internet horror story format that spread through online communities before being adapted into a feature film. Obsession, made for $750,000, brought in matching box office returns on its opening weekend.

Both films drew audiences primarily through their existing YouTube fan bases rather than conventional marketing campaigns. The production costs for both projects came in well below typical Hollywood studio budgets, which typically range from $50 million to over $200 million for major releases.

The results have prompted discussions across the entertainment industry about changing distribution patterns. Traditional studios spend tens of millions on marketing campaigns alongside their substantial production budgets. The success of these YouTube-originated projects suggests audiences will pay for theatrical experiences based on content they discovered online, regardless of promotional spending.

Industry analysts note the results could influence how studios evaluate projects and allocate resources. Both Backrooms and Obsession benefited from years of community building on YouTube before their theatrical releases, a timeline that differs significantly from traditional film development and marketing cycles. This established fanbase proved more valuable than expensive promotional campaigns in driving opening weekend attendance.

The shift reflects broader changes in how younger audiences discover and consume entertainment. Generation Z viewers increasingly find content through digital platforms rather than traditional media channels. These YouTube creators had already built loyal audiences eager to see their work on the big screen, eliminating the need for extensive studio marketing efforts.

The success of these lower-budget horror films contrasts with the massive spending typical of studio blockbusters. While major film productions allocate enormous budgets to both creation and promotion, the YouTube-originated films achieved comparable or superior opening weekend returns with minimal marketing investment.

The theatrical releases represent a natural progression for content creators who had already developed substantial followings online. Rather than starting from scratch with unknown projects, these filmmakers brought existing communities into theaters, bypassing the traditional path of building awareness through advertising and publicity campaigns.

Moving forward, studios may reconsider how they identify and develop projects. The box office performance of Backrooms and Obsession demonstrates that online popularity can serve as a reliable indicator of theatrical demand. This could lead to increased investment in adapting successful online content and recruiting digital creators with proven audience loyalty, fundamentally changing how the entertainment industry discovers and develops new films.

cards.headline: Tom Holland Delayed Spider-Man Film to Star in Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey
cards.teaser: The actor called Sony Pictures to postpone production of Spider-Man: Brand New Day after Nolan offered him a role in the epic.
cards.body:
Tom Holland revealed in GQ magazine that he had a difficult conversation with Sony Pictures boss Tom Rothman about postponing Spider-Man: Brand New Day. The delay enabled Holland to accept Christopher Nolan's offer to appear in The Odyssey instead of having to choose between the two projects.

Holland, who appears on GQ's summer cover for The Odyssey, described the initial discussion with Rothman as challenging. The production schedule adjustment ultimately allowed the actor to commit to both films.

cards.headline: Tribeca Festival to Premiere AI-Generated Film About Iranian Protests
cards.teaser: Festival co-founder Jane Rosenthal defended the decision to show Dreams of Violets, created entirely using artificial intelligence.
cards.body:
Tribeca Film Festival co-founder Jane Rosenthal defended the festival's decision to premiere Dreams of Violets, a fully AI-generated film about the Iranian civilian resistance. Speaking at the festival's 25th anniversary cocktail reception in lower Manhattan, Rosenthal said people need to read the director's statement and that the film should be seen right now at this time.

Director Ash Koosha is Iranian. The film covers protests and civilian resistance in Iran. Rosenthal made her comments to Variety, addressing what she characterized as a need for audiences to understand the director's perspective on the project.

cards.headline: Netflix UK Unscripted Chief Says AI Should Not Be Used in Reality Shows
cards.teaser: Syeda Irtizaali said it is hard now to tell what is fake and what is real when artificial intelligence enters unscripted television.
cards.body:
Syeda Irtizaali, Netflix's UK director of unscripted content, cautioned against using artificial intelligence in reality television during a talk at SXSW London. She highlighted the growing difficulty in distinguishing authentic footage from AI-manipulated content in the reality TV space.

While Irtizaali acknowledged Netflix's tech-forward approach and welcomed AI as a brainstorming tool, she drew a clear boundary around its application in production. The executive firmly stated she does not want artificial intelligence involved in the actual creation of unscripted television programs.

cards.headline: BTS to Headline iHeartRadio Festival in Las Vegas
cards.teaser: The group will return to the city as headliners for the two-day event in September.
cards.body:
BTS will headline the iHeartRadio Festival in Las Vegas, marking another major appearance by the group in the city. The two-day event is scheduled for September. The festival will also feature performances by Cardi B, Lainey Wilson, Benson Boone, and Zara Larsson.

The announcement continues BTS's pattern of large-scale appearances in Las Vegas, where the group has previously performed. Additional performers for the September festival include several artists across different genres.

cards.headline: Motion Picture Association to Honor Hunger Games Director Francis Lawrence
cards.teaser: Lawrence will receive the 2026 MPA Creator Award for his work across multiple film franchises.
cards.body:
The Motion Picture Association will honor Francis Lawrence with its 2026 MPA Creator Award. Lawrence directed five films in the Hunger Games franchise and The Long Walk, an adaptation of a Stephen King novel that performed well at the box office when it opened last fall.

Lawrence's other credits include I Am Legend. The director has worked across multiple major franchises and literary adaptations throughout his career. The MPA Creator Award recognizes filmmakers for their contributions to the industry.

cards.headline: Death Cab for Cutie Returns to Indie Label for New Album
cards.teaser: Ben Gibbard and Dave Depper say the band's anniversary tour and label change shaped their new record I Built You a Tower.
cards.body:
Death Cab for Cutie band members Ben Gibbard and Dave Depper described how the band's anniversary tour and return to an indie label influenced their new album I Built You a Tower. The musicians told interviewers the band is not messing around with their latest work.

The group used their past catalog and touring experience as reference points while creating the new material. The return to an independent record label marked a change in the band's distribution approach after previous major label releases.

hero.headline: Trump names housing regulator Bill Pulte acting director of national intelligence
hero.body:
President Trump has appointed Bill Pulte, head of the Federal Housing Finance Agency, to serve as acting director of national intelligence. Pulte will retain his position overseeing the FHFA while taking on one of the nation's most sensitive security roles.

The appointment came days after Tulsi Gabbard departed from the intelligence director position. Trump announced the decision on his Truth Social platform, stating that "William has deep experience managing the most sensitive matters in America."

Pulte, an heir to a home construction company fortune and major Republican donor, has no known background in national security or intelligence work. His prominence in the Trump administration stems from his role at the FHFA, the agency that regulates Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, which together back approximately half of all U.S. mortgages.

During his tenure at the housing agency, Pulte has made public allegations against several of Trump's political opponents. He has accused Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook of mortgage fraud, charges Cook has denied. He also played a role in Trump's campaign against former Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell.

The dual appointment represents an extraordinary concentration of responsibility. The director of national intelligence coordinates work across 18 intelligence agencies and serves as the president's primary intelligence adviser. The position, created after the September 11 attacks to improve coordination across the intelligence community, has historically demanded exclusive focus given its scope and sensitivity.

Democratic Senator Mark Warner, vice-chairman of the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, criticized the appointment. "Rather than selecting a respected national security professional capable of delivering independent judgments, the president has chosen an official who has demonstrated not just willingness but eagerness to use the authorities of government to pursue political retribution," Warner said.

Warner noted that Pulte had used his FHFA authority to pursue what he characterized as the president's grievances. "Americans have already seen Mr Pulte use the powers of his office at the Federal Housing Finance Agency to pursue the president's perceived political opponents," Warner stated.

A former high-ranking official described Pulte's handling of the Cook case as "very bizarre."

The appointment occurs as the administration manages multiple foreign policy challenges, including ongoing negotiations with Iran and questions surrounding Taiwan policy. Gabbard, during her time as intelligence director, faced marginalization in the role and appeared sidelined as Trump pursued aggressive foreign policy actions.

Pulte's appointment as acting intelligence director while continuing to lead the FHFA means he will simultaneously oversee housing finance policy and manage relationships with the nation's intelligence agencies and foreign intelligence services.

cards.headline: Secretary of State Rubio to testify before Congress as Iran ceasefire deteriorates
cards.teaser: Marco Rubio will appear publicly for the first time since hostilities began, facing lawmakers frustrated with the worsening regional conflict.
cards.body:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio will testify before Congress as the ceasefire agreement with Iran shows signs of collapse. The appearance marks his first public testimony since the war began.

The regional conflict has intensified in recent days, testing the patience of lawmakers who are demanding answers about the administration's strategy. Rubio's testimony comes at a moment when diplomatic efforts to maintain the ceasefire appear to be failing.

cards.headline: Doctors examined Biden immediately after debate amid stroke concerns, new book reveals
cards.teaser: Jill Biden's memoir discloses that medical professionals checked the president right after his debate performance, contradicting earlier official statements.
cards.body:
Former First Lady Jill Biden's upcoming book reveals that doctors examined President Biden immediately after his debate performance against Trump. She had been concerned he might have suffered a stroke.

This account contradicts the Biden administration's previous public statements, which indicated medical examinations took place days after the debate rather than right away. Biden's debate performance had prompted significant questions at the time, and the new details from the former first lady's book provide a different timeline of events than what was previously communicated.

cards.headline: Trump endorses Rep. Tom Kean Jr. despite months-long absence from Congress
cards.teaser: The president backed the New Jersey congressman ahead of an uncontested primary, though Kean has not appeared on Capitol Hill or the campaign trail in months.
cards.body:
President Trump endorsed Rep. Tom Kean Jr. of New Jersey on Monday, calling him a "Great Representative" who "will never let you down." The endorsement came ahead of Tuesday's Republican primary in the state's 7th Congressional District.

Kean has been absent from Capitol Hill and the campaign trail for months leading up to the primary election.

cards.headline: Homeland Security chief backtracks on plan to remove customs officers from airports
cards.teaser: Secretary Markwayne Mullin said he can still initiate the withdrawal of CBP agents but sees no current need to do so in Newark.
cards.body:
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said at a press conference in Dallas that he retains the ability to initiate removal of customs officers from international airports, though he currently sees no need to do so in Newark. The remarks suggest a retreat from an earlier proposal to pull Customs and Border Protection agents from airport posts.

Mullin's comments indicate he is stepping back from the plan he previously floated. While maintaining that he could still implement the removal if needed, his statement that there is no current necessity in Newark represents a shift in position.

cards.headline: Securities and Exchange Commission defends settlement agreement with Elon Musk
cards.teaser: The agency told a judge the $1.5 million deal over Musk's delayed Twitter stake disclosure reflected necessary compromises.
cards.body:
The Securities and Exchange Commission defended its settlement with Elon Musk after a judge questioned the agreement. The SEC reached a deal with Musk in May requiring him to pay $1.5 million over his delayed disclosure of his stake in Twitter, now called X.

In its defense filed with the court, the SEC said the settlement reflected compromises made during negotiations. The case centered on Musk's failure to timely disclose his accumulation of Twitter shares before his eventual takeover bid for the social media platform.

cards.headline: Jon Stewart criticizes Trump over stalled Iran negotiations
cards.teaser: The comedian questioned the president's dealmaking abilities as peace talks fail to produce an agreement.
cards.body:
Original Card Text (Unchanged)

Jon Stewart mocked President Trump on Comedy Central's The Daily Show for failing to negotiate a peace deal with Iran. Stewart said Americans had been under the mistaken impression that Trump was "some kind of dealmaker-in-chief."

The host suggested that expectations for a resolution to what he called the "U.S.-Iran kerfuffle" have not been met. Stewart's comments came as diplomatic efforts between the United States and Iran have failed to produce a breakthrough agreement.

---

Note: The additional source material provided discusses related Iran negotiations context but does not contain verified details about Stewart's specific comments or The Daily Show segment that would allow me to rewrite the card with greater specificity. The original card accurately captures the core story from the available sources.
